- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–4% to account for risk premium or reversal.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a “cool-down” correction: reduce forecast by 2–5% for the following 3–7 days.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline after peak), model tends to lag; add 1–3 days of lagged correction to forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model underperforms when sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67); use sentiment-weighted average of recent 7-day mean + 10% buffer if sentiment >0.5.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.5 → -0.5 → +0.5), model often misreads momentum; apply 2–4 day “sentiment filter” to dampen momentum-driven forecasts.
